subject.title: Gateway becomes slow or times out under multi-session / multi-agent load

question: Should this issue remain the broad Gateway multi-session load tracker, or should maintainers split it into narrower raw-transcript, sessions.list, compaction, and live-soak follow-ups now that several partial fixes have landed?
rationale: The remaining evidence spans performance architecture and storage-retention policy rather than one safe mechanical bug fix, and a narrower raw-transcript canonical issue already owns part of the problem.

options.title: Keep broad tracker
options.body: Use this issue to require end-to-end heavy-workload proof across Gateway RPCs, session/history IO, and channel delivery before closure.

options.title: Split into scoped follow-ups
options.body: Move remaining raw transcript policy to https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/66360 and open or link separate profiled issues for any non-transcript RPC hot paths.

options.title: Close after targeted proof
options.body: Close only if maintainers produce current-main or release soak evidence showing the reporter’s multi-agent workload no longer stalls Gateway RPC or delivery.

recommendation.title: Keep broad tracker
recommendation.body: Use this issue to require end-to-end heavy-workload proof across Gateway RPCs, session/history IO, and channel delivery before closure.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent has current-main and release-history signals near the Gateway/session area and is the best available routing owner from the inspected history.
